fieldValues.title: A holon driver session holds no seat, so clerk claim refuses it and earlier holons claimed under the owner's actor
fieldValues.summary: Driving holon semanticops.com#49, this local Claude Code session ran clerk claim srs-web#639 --as builder. As agent:claude-code it was refused ("does not hold the builder seat in WG Agent-supported editor"). The precedent on #591 and #622 was a claim recorded as human:the-greenman by a session acting for the owner; repeating that was refused by the session's permission check as acting under the owner's identity. The owner's answer: the driver is us. The items were claimed openly as agent:claude-code, driver of #49, by label and claim comment, outside clerk claim.
evidence: srs-web#591 claim comment: Claimed by human:the-greenman as builder (a local session driving semanticops.com#43)
clerk claim srs-web#640 --as builder --dry-run, 2026-10-29: claude-code does not hold the builder seat in WG Agent-supported editor
srs-web#639, #640 claim comments, 2026-10-29: Claimed by agent:claude-code as builder, the driver of holon #49
owner, vignette in conversation f100f41a: Is that not us? What is our holon?
fieldValues.body:
- The holon practice (handbook, Driving a unit (holon) to delivery) names a driver, but clerk claim only knows group seats, so the driver has no way to claim through the tool.
- Claiming under the owner's actor makes the record say the owner claimed it; the honest record is the session's own actor, named as driver of the holon.
- Suggested change: clerk claim accepts --as driver when the issue's parent is a Unit (in progress) whose body names the actor as driver.
